subject.title: openclaw-hooks child processes accumulate under load, causing event-loop starvation and message delivery failures

question: Should the long-lived-process report remain a separate lifecycle investigation until an instrumented trace proves whether https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94515 also fixes it?
rationale: The open PR reduces idle PreToolUse fan-out, but current evidence does not establish that fan-out is the reason relay processes survive the already-shipped five-second lifetime bound.

options.title: Require lifecycle trace
options.body: Keep this issue separate and collect event/PID/process-group/timeout evidence before selecting or extending a fix.

options.title: Fold into fan-out work
options.body: Treat the issue as another manifestation of PreToolUse fan-out and require the open PR to prove both reduced process creation and bounded process lifetime.

options.title: Create a broader lifecycle fix
options.body: Sponsor a combined relay concurrency and process-group termination change across all Codex native hook events before further reproduction.

recommendation.title: Require lifecycle trace
recommendation.body: Keep this issue separate and collect event/PID/process-group/timeout evidence before selecting or extending a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and recently maintained the relay registration, timeout, and forced-exit implementation that must be traced.
